weeks.title: Number systems and sets
weeks.summary: Is week tum number systems (ℕ, ℤ, ℚ, ℝ) aur sets ki basic language seekhoge — union, intersection, subsets aur Venn diagram wale counting questions.
concepts: **Natural numbers (ℕ)** counting numbers hain: 0, 1, 2, 3, ... (kuch books 1 se start karti hain, isliye apne course ka convention yaad rakho). **Integers (ℤ)** me negative numbers bhi aa jaate hain.
**Rational numbers (ℚ)** wo hain jo p/q form me likhe ja sakein, jahan p, q integers aur q ≠ 0. Inka decimal ya to terminate hota hai ya repeat hota hai, jaise 0.25 ya 0.333...
**Irrational numbers** jaise √2, √7, π ka decimal na khatam hota hai na repeat hota hai. Rational aur irrational milkar **Real numbers (ℝ)** banate hain: ℕ ⊆ ℤ ⊆ ℚ ⊆ ℝ.
**Set** well-defined objects ka collection hai. Roster form me elements list karte hain {2, 4, 6}, aur set-builder form me rule likhte hain {x | x even hai, 0 < x < 8}.
**Subset**: A ⊆ B ka matlab A ka har element B me bhi hai. n elements wale set ke 2ⁿ subsets hote hain, jisme empty set ∅ aur khud wo set dono count hote hain.
**Set operations**: A ∪ B me dono sets ke saare elements, A ∩ B me sirf common elements, A − B me wo elements jo A me hain par B me nahi. Complement Aᶜ = U − A, jahan U universal set hai.
**Inclusion-exclusion**: |A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| − |A ∩ B|. Common elements do baar count ho jaate hain, isliye ek baar minus karte hain.
**Power set** P(A) matlab A ke saare subsets ka set. Agar |A| = n hai to |P(A)| = 2ⁿ.

example.problem: Ek class me 60 students hain. 35 ko Python pasand hai, 28 ko Excel pasand hai, aur 10 ko dono pasand hain. Kitne students ko dono me se kuch bhi pasand nahi hai?
steps: Maan lo P = Python wale students, E = Excel wale students. Given: |P| = 35, |E| = 28, |P ∩ E| = 10.
Kam se kam ek pasand karne wale = |P ∪ E| = |P| + |E| − |P ∩ E|.
Jinko kuch pasand nahi = total − |P ∪ E| = 60 − 53 = 7.
Answer: **7 students** ko na Python pasand hai na Excel.

mistakes: |A ∪ B| nikalte waqt sirf |A| + |B| jod dena — intersection ko minus karna mat bhoolo, warna common log do baar gin liye jaate hain.
Subsets count karte waqt empty set ∅ ya poore set ko chhod dena. Total subsets 2ⁿ hote hain; proper subsets (set khud ko chhod ke) 2ⁿ − 1.
22/7 ko irrational samajhna. 22/7 to p/q form me hai, isliye rational hai — ye sirf π ka approximation hai, π nahi.
revision: ℕ ⊆ ℤ ⊆ ℚ ⊆ ℝ; irrational = ℝ − ℚ.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa number irrational hai?
questions.explanation: √7 kisi integer ka square nahi hai, isliye iska decimal na terminate hota hai na repeat — ye irrational hai. 0.333... = 1/3 aur √16 = 4 rational hain. 22/7 bhi rational hai; log ise π samajh kar galti karte hain.

questions.question: A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} aur B = {4, 5, 6, 7} hai. A − B kya hoga?
questions.explanation: A − B me wo elements aate hain jo A me hain par B me nahi: 1, 2, 3. {6, 7} to B − A hai, aur {4, 5} intersection hai. {1, 2, 3, 6, 7} symmetric difference hai, wo alag concept hai.

questions.question: Set {a, b, c, d} ke total kitne subsets hain?
questions.explanation: 4 elements hain, to subsets = 2⁴ = 16 (∅ aur poora set dono included). 15 proper subsets ki count hai — trap yahi hai. 8 = 2³ galat power hai.

questions.question: 100 logon ke survey me 45 log Hindi newspaper padhte hain, 60 English newspaper padhte hain, aur 20 dono padhte hain. Kitne log kam se kam ek newspaper padhte hain?
questions.explanation: |H ∪ E| = 45 + 60 − 20 = 85. Agar intersection minus nahi kiya to 105 aata hai, jo total logon se bhi zyada hai. 15 un logon ki count hai jo koi newspaper nahi padhte.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: Har rational number ek integer hai
Har integer ek rational number hai
questions.explanation: Koi bhi integer n ko n/1 likh sakte hain, isliye har integer rational hai (ℤ ⊆ ℚ). Ulta sahi nahi: 1/2 rational hai par integer nahi. √2 irrational hai, aur ℝ me irrationals bhi hain, isliye ℝ ⊆ ℚ galat hai.

questions.question: U = {1, 2, 3, ..., 10}. A = U ke even numbers, B = U ke multiples of 3. |(A ∪ B)ᶜ| kitna hai?
questions.explanation: A = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}, B = {3, 6, 9}. A ∪ B = {2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10} — 7 elements (6 sirf ek baar). Complement = {1, 5, 7}, yaani 3. Agar 6 ko do baar gina to union 8 lagega aur galat answer 2 aayega; 7 to union ka size hai, complement ka nahi.

weeks.title: Relations and functions
weeks.summary: Cartesian product se relations banana, reflexive/symmetric/transitive check karna, aur samajhna ki function ek special relation kyun hai.
concepts: **Cartesian product** A × B = saare ordered pairs (a, b) jahan a ∈ A, b ∈ B. |A × B| = |A| · |B|, aur (a, b) ≠ (b, a) generally.
**Relation** A se B tak = A × B ka koi bhi subset. Set A par relation matlab A × A ka subset; n elements wale set par 2^(n²) relations possible hain.
**Reflexive**: har a ke liye (a, a) ∈ R. **Symmetric**: (a, b) ∈ R ho to (b, a) ∈ R bhi. **Transitive**: (a, b) aur (b, c) ∈ R ho to (a, c) ∈ R.

**Equivalence relation** = reflexive + symmetric + transitive. Ye set ko alag-alag **equivalence classes** me tod deta hai, jaise integers ko '3 se divide karne par remainder' ke hisaab se 3 groups me.
**Function** f: A → B ek relation hai jisme A ke har element ka exactly ek image ho. Ek input ke do output hon, ya koi input chhoot jaye, to function nahi.
**Domain, codomain, range**: domain = allowed inputs, codomain = jahan outputs aa sakte hain, range = jo outputs actually aate hain. Hamesha range ⊆ codomain.

example.problem: A = {1, 2, 3} par R = {(1,1), (2,2), (3,3), (1,2), (2,1)}. Check karo R equivalence relation hai ya nahi, aur equivalence classes likho.
steps: Reflexive: (1,1), (2,2), (3,3) teeno R me hain, to R reflexive hai.
Symmetric: (1,2) hai to (2,1) bhi hai; baaki pairs (a,a) type ke hain. To R symmetric hai.
Transitive: (1,2) aur (2,1) se (1,1) chahiye — hai. (2,1) aur (1,2) se (2,2) chahiye — hai. (a,a) wale pairs se kuch naya nahi banta. To R transitive hai.
Teeno properties hold karti hain, isliye R equivalence relation hai.
Classes: 1 aur 2 ek doosre se related hain, 3 sirf khud se. Answer: classes **{1, 2}** aur **{3}**.

mistakes: Symmetric check karte waqt sirf ek pair dekhna. Har (a, b) ke liye (b, a) check karo.
Codomain aur range ko same samajhna. f(x) = x² on ℤ → ℤ ka codomain ℤ hai, par range sirf perfect squares hai.
Ek input ke do outputs wale relation ko function maan lena — function me har input ka exactly ek output hona chahiye.
revision: n elements par relations ki count = 2^(n²).
Function: har input ka exactly ek output.

questions.question: A = {1, 2} aur B = {x, y, z}. |A × B| kitna hai?
questions.explanation: |A × B| = |A| · |B| = 2 · 3 = 6 ordered pairs. 5 tab aata hai jab galti se sizes ko jod dete hain — product ke liye multiply karna hota hai.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa relation {1, 2, 3} se {a, b} tak function NAHI hai?
questions.explanation: Teesre option me input 1 ke do outputs hain (a aur b), isliye ye function nahi hai. Pehla option bhi valid function hai — saare inputs ka same output hona allowed hai, bas har input ka ek hi output ho.

questions.question: ℤ par relation R: a R b agar (a − b) 5 se divisible ho. R kis type ka hai?
options: Reflexive aur symmetric, par transitive nahi
questions.explanation: a − a = 0 divisible by 5 (reflexive). a − b divisible ho to b − a = −(a − b) bhi (symmetric). a − b aur b − c dono divisible hon to unka sum a − c bhi divisible (transitive). Isliye equivalence relation; transitive ko check kiye bina chhod dena common trap hai.

questions.question: ℝ par relation R: a R b agar a ≤ b. Inme se kaunsi property R me fail hoti hai?
questions.explanation: a ≤ a hamesha sach (reflexive), a ≤ b aur b ≤ c se a ≤ c (transitive). Par 2 ≤ 5 hai, 5 ≤ 2 nahi — isliye symmetric fail hota hai.

questions.question: f: ℤ → ℤ, f(x) = x². Is function ki range kya hai?
questions.explanation: Integer ka square hamesha perfect square hota hai: 0, 1, 4, 9, ... 'Saare non-negative integers' trap hai, kyunki 2 ya 3 kabhi output nahi aate. Codomain ℤ hai, par range usse chhoti hai.

questions.question: 3 elements wale set A par total kitne alag relations ban sakte hain?
questions.explanation: Relation on A = A × A ka subset. |A × A| = 3 · 3 = 9, isliye subsets = 2⁹ = 512. 9 sirf pairs ki count hai, relations ki nahi; 64 = 2⁶ tab aata hai jab galti se 3 + 3 = 6 pairs maan lete hain.

weeks.title: Coordinate geometry: straight lines
weeks.summary: Points ke beech distance, midpoint, slope, line ki equation, aur parallel/perpendicular lines ki conditions.
concepts: **Distance formula**: P(x₁, y₁) aur Q(x₂, y₂) ke beech distance = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²). Ye Pythagoras theorem hi hai.
**Section formula**: segment ko m:n me internally divide karne wala point = ((m·x₂ + n·x₁)/(m + n), (m·y₂ + n·y₁)/(m + n)). m:n = 1:1 lo to **midpoint** milta hai.
**Slope** m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = tan θ. Horizontal line ka slope 0, vertical line ka slope undefined.
**Parallel** lines ke slopes equal: m₁ = m₂. **Perpendicular** lines me m₁ · m₂ = −1 (agar koi vertical/horizontal na ho).
**Line ke forms**: slope-intercept y = mx + c, point-slope y − y₁ = m(x − x₁), general form ax + by + c = 0 jiska slope −a/b hota hai.
**Intercepts**: x-intercept ke liye y = 0 rakho, y-intercept ke liye x = 0 rakho.
**Point se line ki distance**: (x₀, y₀) se ax + by + c = 0 tak perpendicular distance = |a·x₀ + b·y₀ + c| / √(a² + b²).

example.problem: Points (2, 3) aur (4, 7) se guzarne wali line ki equation aur uske intercepts nikalo.
steps: Point-slope form with (2, 3): y − 3 = 2(x − 2).
Simplify: y = 2x − 4 + 3 = 2x − 1.
y-intercept: x = 0 rakho, y = −1. x-intercept: y = 0 rakho, 2x = 1, x = 1/2.
Answer: **y = 2x − 1** (general form 2x − y − 1 = 0), x-intercept 1/2, y-intercept −1.

mistakes: Slope me order mix karna, jaise (y₂ − y₁)/(x₁ − x₂). Numerator aur denominator me same point pehle lo.
ax + by + c = 0 ka slope a/b likh dena — sahi slope −a/b hai.
Perpendicular slope ko 1/m likhna. Sahi hai −1/m (sign bhi badalta hai).
revision: Slope = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁); ax + by + c = 0 ka slope −a/b.
Parallel: m₁ = m₂; perpendicular: m₁ · m₂ = −1.

questions.question: Points (1, 2) aur (4, 6) ke beech distance kitna hai?
questions.explanation: √((4 − 1)² + (6 − 2)²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5. 25 tab aata hai jab square root lena bhool jaate hain; 7 = 3 + 4 seedha jod dene se aata hai, jo galat hai.

questions.question: Line 3x + 4y − 12 = 0 ka slope kya hai?
questions.explanation: 4y = −3x + 12, to y = −(3/4)x + 3, slope = −3/4. Formula −a/b se bhi −3/4 aata hai. Minus sign bhoolne par 3/4 aata hai, aur a/b ulta karne par −4/3.

questions.question: Line y = 2x + 5 ke perpendicular aur point (0, 1) se guzarne wali line kaunsi hai?
questions.explanation: Given slope 2 hai, perpendicular slope = −1/2. (0, 1) se guzarti hai to y-intercept 1: y = −x/2 + 1. y = 2x + 1 parallel line hai; y = x/2 + 1 me sign change karna bhool gaye.

questions.question: A(1, 2) aur B(7, 8) ko jodne wale segment ko A ki taraf se 1:2 ratio me internally divide karne wala point kaunsa hai?
questions.explanation: m:n = 1:2, point = ((1·7 + 2·1)/3, (1·8 + 2·2)/3) = (9/3, 12/3) = (3, 4). Ye A ke paas hona chahiye kyunki A se distance kam hai. (5, 6) ratio ulta lagane par aata hai, aur (4, 5) midpoint hai.

questions.question: Lines 2x + ky = 5 aur 4x + 6y = 7 parallel hain. k ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Slopes: −2/k aur −4/6 = −2/3. Parallel ke liye −2/k = −2/3, to k = 3. Check: 2x + 3y = 5 ko 2 se multiply karo to 4x + 6y = 10 — same direction, alag line. −3 sign galti se aata hai.

questions.question: Point (3, −2) se line 4x − 3y + 2 = 0 ki perpendicular distance kitni hai?
questions.explanation: |4·3 − 3·(−2) + 2| / √(4² + 3²) = |12 + 6 + 2| / 5 = 20/5 = 4. −3 · (−2) = +6 hota hai; yahan sign galat karne par 8/5 aata hai. Denominator √(a² + b²) bhoolne par 20 aata hai.

weeks.title: Quadratic functions
weeks.summary: Parabola ka shape, vertex, discriminant se roots ka nature, aur roots ke sum-product formulas.
concepts: **Quadratic function**: f(x) = ax² + bx + c, jahan a ≠ 0. Iska graph ek **parabola** hota hai.
a > 0 ho to parabola upar khulta hai aur vertex pe **minimum** value milti hai; a < 0 ho to neeche khulta hai aur vertex pe **maximum**.
**Vertex** ka x-coordinate = −b/(2a). Isi se guzarne wali vertical line x = −b/(2a) **axis of symmetry** hai.
**Discriminant** D = b² − 4ac. D > 0: do alag real roots; D = 0: ek repeated root (graph x-axis ko touch karta hai); D < 0: koi real root nahi.
**Quadratic formula**: x = (−b ± √D) / (2a).
**Roots ka sum aur product**: α + β = −b/a, αβ = c/a.
**Vertex form**: f(x) = a(x − h)² + k, jahan vertex (h, k) hai. Completing the square se ye form milta hai.

example.problem: f(x) = x² − 6x + 5 ka vertex, minimum value aur roots nikalo.
steps: a = 1, b = −6, c = 5. a > 0 hai, to parabola upar khulega aur vertex pe minimum hoga.
Vertex x = −b/(2a) = 6/2 = 3.
f(3) = 9 − 18 + 5 = −4, to vertex (3, −4) aur vertex form (x − 3)² − 4.
D = 36 − 20 = 16 > 0, to do alag real roots.
x = (6 ± 4)/2, yaani x = 5 ya x = 1.
Answer: vertex **(3, −4)**, minimum value **−4**, roots **1 aur 5**.

mistakes: Vertex formula me sign galat lena: x = −b/(2a) hai, b/(2a) nahi.
Max/min value poochi ho to vertex ka x-coordinate likh dena — value ke liye us x ko f(x) me rakhna padta hai.
Product of roots ko −c/a likhna. Sahi hai c/a; sum me minus aata hai (−b/a).
revision: D = b² − 4ac: >0 do roots, =0 ek root, <0 no real root.

questions.question: f(x) = 2x² − 8x + 3 ke vertex ka x-coordinate kya hai?
questions.explanation: x = −b/(2a) = −(−8)/(2·2) = 8/4 = 2. Minus sign chhod dene par −2 aata hai, aur 2a ki jagah sirf a se divide karne par 4.

questions.question: Equation x² + 4x + 7 = 0 ke roots ke baare me kya sahi hai?
options: Ek positive aur ek negative root
questions.explanation: D = 4² − 4·1·7 = 16 − 28 = −12 < 0, isliye koi real root nahi; parabola poora x-axis ke upar hai. Sirf b² positive dekh kar 'do roots' bol dena galat hai — 4ac bhi subtract karna padta hai.

questions.question: f(x) = −x² + 4x + 1 ki maximum value kya hai?
questions.explanation: a = −1 < 0, to vertex pe maximum. x = −4/(2·(−1)) = 2, f(2) = −4 + 8 + 1 = 5. 2 to sirf vertex ka x-coordinate hai, value nahi. −11 tab aata hai jab x = −2 rakh dete ho.

questions.question: Agar α, β equation 2x² − 5x + 3 = 0 ke roots hain, to α + β aur αβ kya hain?
questions.explanation: α + β = −b/a = 5/2, αβ = c/a = 3/2. Check: roots 1 aur 3/2 hain, sum 5/2 aur product 3/2 ✓. Sum me minus bhoolne se −5/2, aur a = 2 se divide na karne par 5 aur 3 aata hai.

questions.question: Equation x² + kx + 9 = 0 ke equal roots hain aur k > 0. k kya hai?
questions.explanation: Equal roots ke liye D = 0: k² − 36 = 0, to k = ±6; k > 0 hai isliye k = 6. 36 = k² hai, k nahi. Tab equation (x + 3)² = 0 banti hai.

questions.question: Ek parabola ka vertex (1, −2) hai aur ye point (3, 6) se guzarta hai. Iski equation kya hai?
questions.explanation: Vertex form: f(x) = a(x − 1)² − 2. (3, 6) rakho: 4a − 2 = 6, to a = 2. f(x) = 2(x − 1)² − 2 = 2x² − 4x. Option 1 me a = 1 maan liya (a nikala hi nahi). 2x² + 4x me (x + 1) liya, yaani vertex ka sign galat.

weeks.title: Algebra of polynomials
weeks.summary: Polynomials ka degree, operations, division algorithm, remainder aur factor theorem, aur roots se graph ka behaviour.
concepts: **Polynomial**: aₙxⁿ + ... + a₁x + a₀, jahan saari powers non-negative integers hain. Sabse badi power = **degree**, aur uska coefficient = **leading coefficient**.
1/x, √x jaise terms polynomial me allowed nahi, par coefficients koi bhi real number ho sakte hain (jaise √3·x²).
**Operations**: addition/subtraction me like terms combine karo. Multiplication me degrees jud jaati hain: deg(p·q) = deg p + deg q.
**Division algorithm**: p(x) = d(x)·q(x) + r(x), jahan r = 0 ya deg r < deg d.
**Remainder theorem**: p(x) ko (x − a) se divide karo to remainder = p(a). (x + a) ke liye p(−a) rakho.
**Factor theorem**: p(a) = 0 ho tabhi (x − a), p(x) ka factor hota hai. Degree n polynomial ke at most n real roots hote hain.
**Graph behaviour**: odd multiplicity root pe graph x-axis cross karta hai, even multiplicity pe touch karke wapas mudta hai. Leading term se pata chalta hai ki dono ends upar jaayenge ya neeche.

steps: Constant term −6 ke factors try karo: ±1, ±2, ±3, ±6.
p(1) = 1 − 6 + 11 − 6 = 0, to factor theorem se (x − 1) factor hai.
Divide karo: p(x) = (x − 1)(x² − 5x + 6).
Check: (x − 1)(x² − 5x + 6) = x³ − 5x² + 6x − x² + 5x − 6 = x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6 ✓.

mistakes: (x + a) se divide karte waqt p(a) rakh dena. Remainder p(−a) hota hai, kyunki x + a = x − (−a).
Subtraction me doosre bracket ke har term ka sign badalna bhool jaana.
Product ki degree ko degrees ka multiplication samajhna — degrees add hoti hain.
revision: Degree n ⇒ at most n real roots, at most n − 1 turning points.
Even multiplicity: touch; odd multiplicity: cross.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa polynomial NAHI hai?
questions.explanation: 2/x = 2x⁻¹, jisme power negative hai, isliye x² + 2/x polynomial nahi. Constant 5 degree 0 ka polynomial hai, aur √3·x² me sirf coefficient irrational hai — power to 2 hi hai, wo allowed hai.

questions.question: (x³ + 2x)(4x² − 1) ki degree kya hai?
questions.explanation: Leading terms ka product x³ · 4x² = 4x⁵, isliye degree 3 + 2 = 5. 6 tab aata hai jab degrees ko multiply kar dete ho.

questions.question: p(x) = 2x³ − 3x² + x − 5 ko (x + 1) se divide karne par remainder kya hoga?
questions.explanation: (x + 1) ke liye x = −1 rakho: 2(−1) − 3(1) + (−1) − 5 = −2 − 3 − 1 − 5 = −11. −5 to p(1) hai, jo (x − 1) se divide karne par aata.

questions.question: Agar (x − 2), x³ − kx + 6 ka factor hai, to k kya hai?
questions.explanation: Factor theorem: p(2) = 0. 8 − 2k + 6 = 0, to 2k = 14, k = 7. Galti se x = −2 rakhne par −8 + 2k + 6 = 0, k = 1 aata hai — trap yahi hai.

questions.question: (x² + 3x − 1) − (2x² − x + 4) ko simplify karo.
questions.explanation: Doosre bracket ka har sign badlo: x² + 3x − 1 − 2x² + x − 4 = −x² + 4x − 5. Agar minus sirf pehle term pe lagaya to −x² + 2x + 3 aata hai — ye sabse common galti hai.

questions.question: p(x) = (x + 1)²(x − 2)(x − 3). Diye gaye x values me se kis par p(x) < 0 hai?
questions.explanation: (x + 1)² kabhi negative nahi hota, to sign (x − 2)(x − 3) se decide hota hai, jo sirf 2 < x < 3 me negative hai. x = 2.5: (3.5)²(0.5)(−0.5) < 0 ✓. x = −2 par p = 1·(−4)(−5) = 20 > 0 — −1 even multiplicity root hai, wahan sign nahi badalta.

weeks.title: One-one, onto and inverse
weeks.summary: Functions ko one-one, onto aur bijective ke hisaab se check karna, inverse nikalna, composition aur graph shifts samajhna.
concepts: **One-one (injective)**: alag inputs ke alag outputs; f(a) = f(b) ⇒ a = b. Graph pe **horizontal line test**: koi bhi horizontal line graph ko ek se zyada baar na kaate.
**Onto (surjective)**: codomain ka har element kisi na kisi input ka output ho, yaani range = codomain.
**Bijective** = one-one + onto. Sirf bijective function ka **inverse** f⁻¹ exist karta hai.
**Inverse nikalne ka tarika**: y = f(x) likho, x ko y ke terms me solve karo, phir x aur y swap karo. Dhyan do: f⁻¹(x) ka matlab 1/f(x) nahi hai.
**Composition**: (g∘f)(x) = g(f(x)) — pehle f, phir g. Generally g∘f ≠ f∘g.
f⁻¹ ka graph, f ke graph ka line y = x me mirror image hota hai.
**Graph transformations**: f(x) + k graph ko k upar le jaata hai, f(x − h) graph ko h right shift karta hai, −f(x) x-axis me reflect karta hai.

example.problem: f: ℝ → ℝ, f(x) = 3x − 4. Dikhao ki f bijective hai aur f⁻¹ nikalo.
steps: One-one: f(a) = f(b) ⇒ 3a − 4 = 3b − 4 ⇒ a = b. To f one-one hai.
Onto: koi bhi y ∈ ℝ lo; x = (y + 4)/3 bhi real hai aur f(x) = y. To f onto hai.
Isliye f bijective hai aur inverse exist karta hai.
y = 3x − 4 ⇒ x = (y + 4)/3. x aur y swap karo.

mistakes: f⁻¹(x) ko 1/f(x) samajhna. Inverse function input-output ko ulta karta hai, reciprocal nahi leta.
Onto check karte waqt codomain ignore karna. f(x) = eˣ, ℝ → ℝ par onto nahi hai, par ℝ → (0, ∞) par onto hai.
Composition ka order ulta lena: (g∘f)(x) me pehle f lagta hai, g baad me.
revision: f(x − h) + k: h right, k up.

questions.question: f: ℝ → ℝ, f(x) = x². Ye function kaisa hai?
questions.explanation: f(2) = f(−2) = 4, to one-one nahi. Negative numbers (jaise −1) kabhi output nahi aate, to codomain ℝ par onto bhi nahi. Domain [0, ∞) aur codomain [0, ∞) karne par hi ye bijective banta hai.

questions.question: f(x) = 2x + 1 aur g(x) = x². (g∘f)(1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: (g∘f)(1) = g(f(1)) = g(3) = 9. 3 tab aata hai jab order ulta karke (f∘g)(1) = f(1) = 3 nikal lete ho.

questions.question: f(x) = (x − 5)/2 ka inverse function kya hai?
questions.explanation: y = (x − 5)/2 ⇒ 2y = x − 5 ⇒ x = 2y + 5. Swap karke f⁻¹(x) = 2x + 5. Check: f(f⁻¹(1)) = f(7) = 1 ✓. 2/(x − 5) reciprocal hai, inverse nahi.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa function f: ℝ → ℝ bijective hai?
questions.explanation: x³ strictly increasing hai (one-one) aur har real number ka cube root real hai (onto). eˣ one-one hai par negative values ya 0 kabhi nahi deta, isliye ℝ par onto nahi — ye sabse common trap hai. x² aur |x| one-one hi nahi.

questions.question: y = (x − 3)² + 2 ka graph, y = x² ke graph ko kaise shift karke milta hai?
questions.explanation: f(x − 3) graph ko 3 units right le jaata hai (minus dekh kar left mat socho), aur + 2 graph ko 2 units upar. Vertex (0, 0) se (3, 2) pe chala jaata hai.

questions.question: f(x) = 2x + 3 aur g(x) = x − 1. (f∘g)⁻¹(7) kya hai?
questions.explanation: (f∘g)(x) = f(x − 1) = 2(x − 1) + 3 = 2x + 1. (f∘g)⁻¹(7) matlab wo x jiske liye 2x + 1 = 7, yaani x = 3. Doosra tarika: g⁻¹(f⁻¹(7)) = g⁻¹(2) = 3. Order ulta lene par f⁻¹(g⁻¹(7)) = 5/2 aata hai; 15 to (f∘g)(7) hai.

weeks.title: Exponentials and logarithms
weeks.summary: Exponential growth/decay functions, logarithm as inverse, log ke rules, aur exponential/log equations solve karna.
concepts: **Exponential function**: f(x) = aˣ, jahan a > 0 aur a ≠ 1. Domain ℝ, range (0, ∞), aur graph hamesha (0, 1) se guzarta hai.
a > 1 ho to function increasing (**growth**), 0 < a < 1 ho to decreasing (**decay**).
**Exponent rules**: aᵐ · aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ, aᵐ / aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ, (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ, a⁰ = 1, a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ.
**Logarithm**: logₐ(x) = y ka matlab aʸ = x. Log, exponential ka inverse hai; iska domain (0, ∞) hai aur logₐ(1) = 0.
**Log rules**: log(xy) = log x + log y, log(x/y) = log x − log y, log(xⁿ) = n · log x. Par log(x + y) ka koi aisa rule nahi hai.
**Change of base**: logₐ(x) = ln(x) / ln(a). **ln** natural log hai jiska base e ≈ 2.718 hai.
Growth model: A = P(1 + r)ᵗ. Kitne time me value double hogi, ye log se nikalte hain.

steps: Domain check: x > 0 aur x − 2 > 0, to x > 2 chahiye.
Product rule: log₂(x(x − 2)) = 3.
Exponential form: x(x − 2) = 2³ = 8.
x = −2 domain (x > 2) me nahi hai, isliye reject.
Check: log₂4 + log₂2 = 2 + 1 = 3 ✓. Answer: **x = 4**.

mistakes: log(x + y) = log x + log y likh dena. Rule product ke liye hai: log(xy) = log x + log y.
Log equation solve karke domain check na karna — negative ya zero ka log defined nahi hota, aise roots reject karo.
logₐ(x) aur logₓ(a) ko same samajhna; ye ek doosre ke reciprocal hain.
revision: log(xy) = log x + log y; log(xⁿ) = n log x.
aˣ ki range (0, ∞); log ka domain (0, ∞).

questions.question: log₂(64) ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: 2⁶ = 64, isliye log₂(64) = 6. 8 tab aata hai jab √64 le lete ho, aur 32 jab 64/2 kar dete ho — log ka matlab 'kaunsi power' hai.

questions.question: f(x) = (1/2)ˣ ke baare me kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: Iski range (0, ∞) hai aur ye decreasing hai
Iski range saare real numbers hai
questions.explanation: Base 1/2 < 1 hai, isliye function decreasing hai, aur aˣ hamesha positive hota hai, to range (0, ∞). Graph (0, 1) se guzarta hai, (1, 0) se nahi — (1, 0) to log graph ka point hai.

questions.question: log₁₀(50) + log₁₀(2) ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Product rule: log(50) + log(2) = log(100) = 2, kyunki 10² = 100. log(52) trap hai — logs add karne par numbers multiply hote hain, add nahi. 100 andar wali value hai, log nahi.

questions.question: Solve karo: 3^(2x − 1) = 27.
questions.explanation: 27 = 3³, to 2x − 1 = 3, 2x = 4, x = 2. Check: 3³ = 27 ✓. x = 14 tab aata hai jab 2x − 1 = 27 likh dete ho (base same karna bhool gaye); 3/2 tab jab −1 ignore kar diya.

questions.question: log₄(8) ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: 4ʸ = 8 ⇒ 2^(2y) = 2³ ⇒ 2y = 3 ⇒ y = 3/2. Change of base se bhi: log₂8 / log₂4 = 3/2. 2/3 tab aata hai jab fraction ulta likh dete ho, yaani log₈(4).

questions.question: Solve karo: log₃(x) + log₃(x − 8) = 2.
questions.explanation: log₃(x(x − 8)) = 2 ⇒ x² − 8x = 9 ⇒ x² − 8x − 9 = 0 ⇒ (x − 9)(x + 1) = 0. x = −1 par log₃(−1) defined nahi, isliye reject. Sirf x = 9: log₃9 + log₃1 = 2 + 0 = 2 ✓. Dono roots rakh lena main trap hai.

weeks.title: Sequences and limits
weeks.summary: AP aur GP ke formulas, sequence ka convergence, function ke limits nikalne ke tarike, aur continuity ka matlab.
concepts: **Sequence**: numbers ki ordered list a₁, a₂, a₃, ..., jise nth term formula aₙ se describe karte hain.
**AP (Arithmetic Progression)**: aₙ = a + (n − 1)d, aur first n terms ka sum Sₙ = (n/2)[2a + (n − 1)d].
**GP (Geometric Progression)**: aₙ = a · rⁿ⁻¹. |r| < 1 ho to infinite sum = a/(1 − r); |r| ≥ 1 par infinite sum finite nahi hota.
**Convergent sequence**: n → ∞ par aₙ kisi fixed number L ke paas pahunchta hai, jaise 1/n → 0. Warna **divergent**, jaise aₙ = n ya (−1)ⁿ.
**Limit of a function**: lim(x→a) f(x) = L matlab x ko a ke bahut kareeb le jao to f(x), L ke kareeb aata hai. Left-hand aur right-hand limits equal hone chahiye.
**0/0 form**: seedha value rakhne par 0/0 aaye to factorise karke common factor cancel karo, phir value rakho.
**x → ∞ par rational function**: numerator aur denominator ko highest power se divide karo. Degrees equal hon to limit = leading coefficients ka ratio.
**Continuity**: f, x = a par continuous hai agar lim(x→a) f(x) exist kare aur f(a) ke barabar ho.

steps: Seedha x = 3 rakho: (9 − 9)/(3 − 3) = 0/0, ye indeterminate form hai.
Numerator factorise karo: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3).
x → 3 me x ≠ 3, isliye (x − 3) cancel kar sakte hain: expression = x + 3.
Ab x = 3 rakho: 3 + 3 = 6.
Answer: limit = **6**. (Function x = 3 par defined nahi hai, phir bhi limit exist karti hai.)

mistakes: 0/0 aate hi 'limit exist nahi karti' bol dena. 0/0 ka matlab hai aur kaam karo — factorise ya simplify karo.
AP ka nth term a + nd likh dena. Sahi hai a + (n − 1)d, kyunki pehle term me d add nahi hota.
|r| ≥ 1 wali GP par bhi a/(1 − r) laga dena — ye formula sirf |r| < 1 ke liye hai.
revision: GP: aₙ = a·rⁿ⁻¹, S∞ = a/(1 − r) for |r| < 1.
Continuous at a: LHL = RHL = f(a).

questions.question: AP 4, 7, 10, ... ka 10th term kya hai?
questions.explanation: a = 4, d = 3: a₁₀ = 4 + (10 − 1)·3 = 4 + 27 = 31. 34 tab aata hai jab a + nd = 4 + 30 use kar lete ho.

questions.question: lim(n→∞) 1/n kya hai?
questions.explanation: n jitna bada hota hai, 1/n utna 0 ke paas jaata hai (1/1000, 1/1000000, ...). Ye kabhi exactly 0 nahi banta, par limit 0 hi hai — limit me 'kareeb pahunchna' hi kaafi hai.

questions.question: lim(x→2) (x² − 4)/(x − 2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Seedha rakhne par 0/0. x² − 4 = (x − 2)(x + 2), cancel karke x + 2, aur x = 2 par 4. 0/0 dekh kar 'limit exist nahi karti' bolna galat hai.

questions.question: Infinite GP 6 + 3 + 3/2 + 3/4 + ... ka sum kya hai?
questions.explanation: a = 6, r = 1/2 (|r| < 1). S∞ = 6/(1 − 1/2) = 6/(1/2) = 12. 10.5 sirf pehle teen terms ka sum hai, aur infinite terms ka matlab infinite sum nahi hota jab r chhota ho.

questions.question: lim(x→∞) (3x² + 5)/(2x² − x) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Upar-neeche x² se divide karo: (3 + 5/x²)/(2 − 1/x). x → ∞ par 5/x² → 0 aur 1/x → 0, to limit = 3/2. Degrees equal hain, isliye answer leading coefficients ka ratio hai — 0 ya ∞ nahi.

questions.question: f(x) = x + 1 jab x < 1, aur f(x) = 3x − k jab x ≥ 1. f, x = 1 par continuous ho, iske liye k kya hona chahiye?
questions.explanation: Left-hand limit = 1 + 1 = 2. Right side aur f(1) = 3 − k. Continuity ke liye 3 − k = 2, to k = 1. k = 2 tab aata hai jab LHL hi ko k samajh lete ho.

weeks.title: Derivatives
weeks.summary: Derivative as rate of change aur tangent slope, differentiation rules, tangent line ki equation, aur maxima-minima nikalna.
concepts: **Derivative**: f′(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x + h) − f(x)]/h. Ye kisi point pe function ka instantaneous rate of change hai, yaani tangent line ka slope.
**Power rule**: d/dx(xⁿ) = n·xⁿ⁻¹. Constant ka derivative 0, aur d/dx(c·f) = c·f′.
**Product rule**: (uv)′ = u′v + uv′. **Quotient rule**: (u/v)′ = (u′v − uv′)/v².
**Chain rule**: d/dx f(g(x)) = f′(g(x)) · g′(x) — bahar wale ka derivative, andar wale ka derivative se multiply.
**Standard results**: (eˣ)′ = eˣ, (ln x)′ = 1/x (x > 0).
**Tangent line** x = a par: y − f(a) = f′(a)(x − a).
**Increasing/decreasing**: f′ > 0 to increasing, f′ < 0 to decreasing. **Critical points** wahan jahan f′(x) = 0.
**Second derivative test**: critical point par f″ > 0 to local minimum, f″ < 0 to local maximum.

example.problem: f(x) = x³ − 3x² + 4 ke local maximum aur local minimum nikalo.
steps: Critical points: f′(x) = 0 ⇒ x = 0 ya x = 2.
x = 0: f″(0) = −6 < 0, to local maximum; f(0) = 4.
Answer: local max **4** (x = 0 par), local min **0** (x = 2 par).

mistakes: Product ka derivative u′ · v′ likh dena. Sahi product rule u′v + uv′ hai.
Chain rule me andar wale function ka derivative multiply karna bhoolna, jaise (3x + 1)⁵ ka derivative 5(3x + 1)⁴ likh dena.
Local min/max value poochi ho to sirf x batana. Value ke liye f(x) me x rakhna padta hai.
revision: f′ = 0 and f″ > 0 ⇒ min; f″ < 0 ⇒ max.

questions.question: 4x³ − 2x + 7 ka derivative kya hai?
questions.explanation: d/dx(4x³) = 12x², d/dx(−2x) = −2, d/dx(7) = 0. Total 12x² − 2. Constant 7 ko −2 me jod dena (12x² + 5) galat hai, kyunki constant ka derivative 0 hai.

questions.question: Curve y = x² par x = 3 wale point pe tangent ka slope kya hai?
questions.explanation: Slope = f′(3), aur f′(x) = 2x, to f′(3) = 6. 9 to point ka y-coordinate f(3) hai, slope nahi.

questions.question: d/dx (x² · eˣ) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Product rule: (x²)′·eˣ + x²·(eˣ)′ = 2x·eˣ + x²·eˣ = eˣ(x² + 2x). 2x·eˣ sirf ek part hai — ye tab aata hai jab galti se (uv)′ = u′v′ jaisa kuch kar dete ho.

questions.question: d/dx (3x + 1)⁵ kya hai?
questions.explanation: Chain rule: 5(3x + 1)⁴ · d/dx(3x + 1) = 5(3x + 1)⁴ · 3 = 15(3x + 1)⁴. 5(3x + 1)⁴ me andar ka derivative 3 bhool gaye; 15(3x + 1)⁵ me power kam karna bhool gaye.

questions.question: Curve y = x² + 1 par x = 1 wale point pe tangent line ki equation kya hai?
questions.explanation: Point: f(1) = 2, to (1, 2). Slope: f′(x) = 2x, f′(1) = 2. Tangent: y − 2 = 2(x − 1) ⇒ y = 2x. Check: x = 1 par y = 2 ✓. y = 2x + 2 point (1, 2) se guzarti hi nahi.

questions.question: f(x) = 2x³ − 9x² + 12x + 1 ki local minimum value kya hai?
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 6x² − 18x + 12 = 6(x − 1)(x − 2), critical points x = 1, 2. f″(x) = 12x − 18: f″(1) = −6 (max), f″(2) = 6 (min). f(2) = 16 − 36 + 24 + 1 = 5. 6 = f(1) local maximum value hai, aur 2 to sirf min ka x-coordinate.

weeks.title: Integrals
weeks.summary: Integration as reverse of differentiation, definite integral se area nikalna, substitution, aur curves ke beech ka area.
concepts: **Indefinite integral (antiderivative)**: ∫f(x) dx = F(x) + C, jahan F′(x) = f(x). Constant C mat bhoolo, kyunki constant ka derivative 0 hota hai.
**Basic rules**: ∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1) + C (n ≠ −1), ∫(1/x) dx = ln|x| + C, ∫eˣ dx = eˣ + C.
**Linearity**: ∫[a·f(x) + b·g(x)] dx = a∫f dx + b∫g dx.
**Definite integral**: ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a). Ye **Fundamental Theorem of Calculus** hai; isme C cancel ho jaata hai.
**Area meaning**: f ≥ 0 ho to ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx, x = a se b tak curve ke neeche ka area hai. x-axis ke neeche wala hissa negative contribute karta hai.
**Riemann sum**: area ko patle rectangles me todkar approx karte hain; rectangles jitne patle, approximation utna exact.
**Area between curves**: ∫ₐᵇ [upper(x) − lower(x)] dx.
**Substitution**: ∫f(g(x))·g′(x) dx me u = g(x) rakho, to ye ∫f(u) du ban jaata hai.

example.problem: Curve y = x² + 1 ke neeche, x = 0 se x = 2 tak ka area nikalo.
steps: x² + 1 hamesha positive hai, to area = ∫₀² (x² + 1) dx.
Antiderivative: F(x) = x³/3 + x.
Answer: area = **14/3 square units** (≈ 4.67).

mistakes: Indefinite integral me + C chhod dena.
Integration me power badhane ke baad (n + 1) se divide karna bhool jaana, jaise ∫x² dx = x³ likh dena.
x-axis ke neeche wale hisse ko bhi positive area maan kar definite integral ka answer dena — definite integral net signed area deta hai.
revision: ∫(1/x) dx = ln|x| + C; ∫eˣ dx = eˣ + C.
Substitution: u = g(x), du = g′(x) dx.

questions.question: ∫(6x² + 2) dx kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∫6x² dx = 6·x³/3 = 2x³, ∫2 dx = 2x. Total 2x³ + 2x + C. 12x to derivative hai, integral nahi. 6x³ me 3 se divide karna bhool gaye.

questions.question: ∫₀³ 2x dx ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Antiderivative x², to 3² − 0² = 9. Geometry se bhi: base 3, height 6 wala triangle, area = (1/2)·3·6 = 9. 6 = f(3) hai, integral nahi; 18 tab aata hai jab 1/2 bhool jaate ho.

questions.question: ∫₁ᵉ (1/x) dx ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∫(1/x) dx = ln x. ln(e) − ln(1) = 1 − 0 = 1. e − 1 tab aata hai jab galti se ∫(1/x) dx = x maan lete ho.

questions.question: x = 0 se x = 1 tak curves y = x aur y = x² ke beech ka area kitna hai?
questions.explanation: 0 < x < 1 me x ≥ x², to upper = x, lower = x². Area = ∫₀¹ (x − x²) dx = 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6. 5/6 tab aata hai jab dono areas subtract ki jagah add kar dete ho.

questions.question: ∫ 2x(x² + 1)³ dx kya hai?
questions.explanation: u = x² + 1, du = 2x dx. Integral = ∫u³ du = u⁴/4 + C = (x² + 1)⁴/4 + C. Check: derivative = 4(x² + 1)³·2x/4 = 2x(x² + 1)³ ✓. 2x ko bahar rakhna galat hai, wo to du me absorb ho gaya.

questions.question: ∫₋₁² (x² − 2x) dx ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: F(x) = x³/3 − x². F(2) = 8/3 − 4 = −4/3, F(−1) = −1/3 − 1 = −4/3. F(2) − F(−1) = 0. Function −1 se 0 tak positive (area 4/3) aur 0 se 2 tak negative (area 4/3) hai, dono cancel. 8/3 total geometric area hai, definite integral nahi.

weeks.title: Graphs, BFS and DFS
weeks.summary: Graph ki basic language, adjacency matrix/list representation, aur graph explore karne ke do tarike — BFS aur DFS — plus DAG me topological order.
concepts: **Graph** G = (V, E): V vertices (nodes) ka set aur E edges (connections) ka set. **Directed graph** me edge u → v ki direction hoti hai.
**Degree**: vertex se judi edges ki count. **Handshaking lemma**: saari degrees ka sum = 2|E|, kyunki har edge do vertices ki degree me count hoti hai.
**Adjacency matrix**: n × n matrix, A[i][j] = 1 agar i se j edge hai. Undirected graph ki matrix symmetric hoti hai.
**Adjacency list**: har vertex ke neighbours ki list. Kam edges wale (sparse) graphs me ye memory bachati hai.
**Complete graph Kₙ**: har pair ke beech edge, total n(n − 1)/2 edges.
**BFS (Breadth First Search)**: queue use karta hai aur level-by-level explore karta hai. Unweighted graph me start se har vertex tak minimum edges wala path deta hai.
**DFS (Depth First Search)**: stack ya recursion use karta hai; ek raaste me jitna deep ja sake jaata hai, phir backtrack karta hai.
**DAG** (directed acyclic graph) ke vertices ko **topological order** me rakh sakte hain: har edge u → v ke liye u, v se pehle aaye.

example.problem: Undirected graph ki edges: A–B, A–C, B–D, C–D, D–E. A se BFS chalao (neighbours alphabetical order me) aur har vertex ka level batao.
steps: Queue = [A], A visited, level(A) = 0.
A nikalo: neighbours B, C add karo. Queue = [B, C], level 1.
B nikalo: neighbour D naya hai, add karo. Queue = [C, D], level(D) = 2.
C nikalo: D pehle hi visited hai, skip. Queue = [D].
D nikalo: E naya hai, add karo, level(E) = 3. Queue = [E].
E nikalo: koi naya neighbour nahi. Queue khaali.
Answer: BFS order **A, B, C, D, E**; levels A = 0, B = C = 1, D = 2, E = 3. A se E tak minimum 3 edges.

mistakes: BFS aur DFS ke data structures mix karna: BFS → queue (FIFO), DFS → stack/recursion (LIFO).
Handshaking lemma me degree sum ko hi edges ki count maan lena — edges = degree sum / 2.
Visited mark na karna, jisse ek vertex queue me do baar aa jaata hai ya cycle me infinite loop.
revision: Undirected adjacency matrix me 1s ki count = 2|E|.
BFS = queue = levels = unweighted shortest path.
DFS = stack/recursion = deep first, then backtrack.
Topological order sirf DAG me possible.

questions.question: Ek undirected graph me 6 vertices hain jinki degrees 2, 3, 3, 2, 4, 2 hain. Graph me kitni edges hain?
questions.explanation: Degree sum = 2 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 4 + 2 = 16 = 2|E|, to |E| = 8. 16 degree sum hai, edges nahi — har edge do baar count hoti hai.

questions.question: BFS graph explore karne ke liye mainly kaunsa data structure use karta hai?
questions.explanation: BFS queue (first in, first out) use karta hai, isliye pehle paas wale (level 1) vertices process hote hain, phir level 2. Stack DFS ke liye hai; priority queue Dijkstra jaise algorithms me aata hai.

questions.question: Complete graph K₆ me kitni edges hain?
questions.explanation: Har pair ke beech ek edge: 6·5/2 = 15. 30 tab aata hai jab 2 se divide nahi karte, yaani har edge ko do baar gin lete ho.

questions.question: Undirected graph ki edges: 1–2, 1–3, 2–4, 3–4, 4–5. Vertex 1 se recursive DFS chalao, neighbours ascending order me. Visit order kya hoga?
questions.explanation: 1 → sabse chhota neighbour 2 → 2 ka unvisited neighbour 4 → 4 ke neighbours 2, 3, 5 me pehla unvisited 3 → 3 ke saare neighbours visited, backtrack to 4 → 5. Order 1, 2, 4, 3, 5. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 BFS ka order hai, DFS ka nahi.

questions.question: 5 vertices aur 7 edges wale undirected simple graph ki adjacency matrix me kitne 1s honge?
questions.explanation: Undirected edge i–j matrix me do jagah 1 deti hai: A[i][j] aur A[j][i]. Isliye 1s = 2 · 7 = 14. 7 tab aata hai jab symmetry bhool jaate ho; 25 to poori matrix ke cells hain.

questions.question: DAG ki edges: A → B, A → C, B → D, C → D, D → E. Inme se kaunsa valid topological order hai?
questions.explanation: Har edge u → v me u pehle aana chahiye. A, C, B, D, E me saari edges follow hoti hain (B aur C ka aapas me order free hai). Pehle option me C → D tootta hai (D, C se pehle), doosre me A → B, aur chauthe me D → E.

weeks.title: Shortest paths and spanning trees
weeks.summary: Weighted graphs me shortest path (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford) aur minimum spanning tree (Prim, Kruskal) nikalna.
concepts: **Weighted graph**: har edge pe ek weight (distance, cost, time). Path ka weight = uski edges ke weights ka sum.

**Dijkstra's algorithm**: single source se shortest paths, jab saare weights non-negative hon. Har step pe sabse kam tentative distance wala unvisited vertex finalize karo aur uske neighbours update karo.
Negative edge weights par Dijkstra galat answer de sakta hai. **Bellman-Ford** negative edges handle karta hai (agar negative cycle na ho) aur negative cycle detect bhi kar sakta hai.
**Floyd-Warshall**: saare vertex pairs ke beech shortest paths ek saath, roughly n³ steps me.
**Tree**: connected graph jisme koi cycle nahi. n vertices wale tree me exactly n − 1 edges hoti hain.
**Spanning tree**: graph ke saare vertices cover karne wala tree. **Minimum spanning tree (MST)** wo spanning tree jiska total weight sabse kam ho.
**Kruskal**: edges ko weight ke increasing order me lo; jo edge cycle na banaye use add karo. **Prim**: ek vertex se start karo, har baar tree se bahar jaane wali sabse sasti edge add karo.

example.problem: Undirected weighted graph: A–B (4), A–C (1), C–B (2), B–D (1), C–D (5). A se Dijkstra chala kar har vertex ki shortest distance nikalo.
steps: Start: d(A) = 0, baaki sab ∞.
A finalize: d(B) = 4, d(C) = 1.
Sabse chhota unvisited C (1) finalize: B via C = 1 + 2 = 3 < 4, to d(B) = 3; D via C = 1 + 5 = 6.
Ab B (3) finalize: D via B = 3 + 1 = 4 < 6, to d(D) = 4.
D (4) finalize. Sab vertices done.
Answer: d(A) = 0, d(C) = **1**, d(B) = **3**, d(D) = **4**; A se D ka path A → C → B → D.

mistakes: Dijkstra me direct edge ko hi final maan lena. A–B ka direct weight 4 tha, par A → C → B sirf 3 hai — har step pe update karo.
Kruskal me cycle check bhool jaana. Sasti edge bhi skip karni padti hai agar wo already connected do vertices ko jodti ho.
Spanning tree me n edges lena. n vertices ke tree me hamesha n − 1 edges hoti hain.
revision: Tree with n vertices ⇒ n − 1 edges.
Bellman-Ford: negative edges OK, negative cycle detect karta hai.
Kruskal: sort edges, add if no cycle.
Prim: grow tree with cheapest outgoing edge.

questions.question: 10 vertices wale kisi bhi tree me kitni edges hoti hain?
questions.explanation: n vertices ke tree me n − 1 edges: 10 − 1 = 9. Ek bhi extra edge cycle bana degi. 45 to complete graph K₁₀ ki edges hain.

questions.question: Dijkstra's algorithm kab galat answer de sakta hai?
options: Jab graph me negative edge weights hon
questions.explanation: Dijkstra ek vertex ko finalize karne ke baad dobara update nahi karta, ye maan kar ki aage ka path sirf lamba hoga. Negative edge ye assumption tod deti hai. Cycles aur undirected graphs me Dijkstra theek kaam karta hai.

questions.question: Undirected weighted graph: S–A (2), S–B (6), A–B (3), A–C (7), B–C (1). S se C ki shortest distance kya hai?
questions.explanation: Dijkstra: d(A) = 2; A se B = 2 + 3 = 5 (< 6); B se C = 5 + 1 = 6; A se C direct = 9. Shortest S → A → B → C = 6. 7 = S → B → C, aur 9 = S → A → C — sirf obvious raaste dekhna trap hai.

questions.question: Graph ki edges: P–Q (1), Q–R (2), P–R (3), R–S (4), Q–S (5), P–S (6). Minimum spanning tree ka total weight kya hai?
questions.explanation: Kruskal: P–Q (1) add, Q–R (2) add, P–R (3) cycle P-Q-R banati hai to skip, R–S (4) add. 4 vertices ke liye 3 edges ho gayi: 1 + 2 + 4 = 7. 10 tab aata hai jab cycle wali edge (3) bhi le lete ho.

questions.question: Kruskal's algorithm kisi edge ko kab skip karta hai?
options: Jab wo edge already chuni hui edges ke saath cycle banaye
Jab uska weight sabse zyada ho
Jab wo kisi naye vertex ko tree se jode
questions.explanation: Kruskal edges ko sasti se mehngi order me dekhta hai aur sirf wahi edge skip karta hai jo cycle bana de. Heavy edge bhi le li jaati hai agar wo do alag components ko jodti ho — sirf weight dekh kar skip karna galat hai.

questions.question: Undirected graph: A–B (3), A–C (1), B–C (7), B–D (5), C–D (2), D–E (4), C–E (6). Prim's algorithm A se start kare to edges kis order me add hongi?
questions.explanation: Tree {A}: sasti edge A–C (1). {A, C}: options A–B 3, C–D 2, C–E 6, C–B 7 → C–D (2). {A, C, D}: A–B 3, D–E 4, D–B 5 → A–B (3). Phir D–E (4). MST weight 10. Doosra option trap hai — Prim sirf A ki edges nahi, poore tree se bahar jaane wali sabse sasti edge leta hai.
